grain: one row per outreach record (a call attempt or an SMS send) for one score; no unique id column, no de-dup possible

columns.name: send_time
columns.meaning: SMS send timestamp; non-null == SMS delivered/sent

columns.name: if_call_suc
columns.meaning: call outcome flag: 1 = connected, 0 = not connected, -1 = not a call (SMS row)

columns.name: score
columns.meaning: model score, all values lie exactly on the 0.001 grid in [0.99, 1.0]

columns.name: score_bucket
columns.meaning: pre-existing 0.001-width bucket label; top bin is written as [0.999,1] and holds BOTH 0.999 and 1.0; all other bins are [A,B)

columns.name: id_bucket
columns.meaning: auxiliary user-attribute bucket (e.g. [40,45), 'other', '[70,70+)'), not needed for this task

score_distribution.note: all scores are multiples of 0.001, so each 0.001-wide bin contains exactly one score value except the top bin

binning_spec_for_downstream.rule: bins of width 0.001 starting at 0.99; 10 bins; every bin [A,B) EXCEPT the highest bin which must be written [A,B] (i.e. [0.999,1]) and absorbs score == 1.0
binning_spec_for_downstream.border_rule: left-closed, right-open for non-top bins (score 0.99 -> '[0.99,0.991)'); top bin closed on both ends, so 0.999 and 1.0 both fall in '[0.999,1]'
binning_spec_for_downstream.float_formatting: format bounds without trailing zeros, matching the file convention: [0.99,0.991), [0.99,0.991) style with %g
binning_spec_for_downstream.verified: labels reproduced this way match the existing score_bucket column on 405777/477049 rows; the only 71272 mismatches are exactly the 0.999 (47572) + 1.0 (23700) rows that belong to the closed top bin -> confirms top-bin-as-[A,B] convention

total.recommended: row count in bucket (calls + SMS records)
total.alt: if the task's 'number of outbound calls' is meant to be total, then total = type=='call' = 225356 rows; downstream should prefer plain row count for 'total' and keep channel split visible via oncall

oncall.ambiguity: AM-1: 87 rows are type=='sms' but if_call_suc==1 (all timestamps null) - they are NOT counted by type=='call'; if 'oncall' is read strictly as if_call_suc != -1 these 87 rows shift from cnt_send/oncall boundary. Use type=='call' unless specified otherwise.

cnt_send.note: SMS rows always have send_time; 90837 call rows also carry a send_time, so cnt_send > #SMS (251693); no click exists without a send_time (click_without_send == 0)

data_quality_findings: Funnel is perfectly nested: click_time non-null => send_time non-null (0 violations); check => apply (0); upgrade => check and => apply (0).

check_time, apply_time and upgrade_time are non-null on exactly the same 182 rows, so cnt_check == cnt_apply == cnt_upgrade for every bucket. Not a bug from the profile's view, but downstream should not be surprised by identical columns.
87 rows (0.018%) have type=='sms' together with if_call_suc==1 and all five timestamps NULL - contradictory channel/outcome flags (anomaly).
No sentinel/placeholder strings: unset timestamps are real NULL, read them with pandas and use isna(), not string comparison.
Single partition dt=20260301 - no date filtering needed.
No id/user column - metrics are record-level counts; no de-duplication possible or required.

score has no nulls and is bounded to [0.99, 1.0]; there are zero rows with score < 0.99, so no 'below-threshold' bin is needed (21,336 rows sit exactly on 0.99 and go into the first bin [0.99,0.991)).
